title: Third hand: premium, with a bigger 3D moment
question: Six new foreign forms, judged against your steer: premium first, plus a bigger 3D moment. The quote grammar leads by the roll. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Name the obvious, in quotes, at giant scale: what is manual, what is automated. One orange tag marks the thing to do.
options.viewport: The headline in huge industrial caps inside straight quotes across a white ground, with a hazard stripe running under the primary action. A WebGL orange zip-tie tag hangs from the nav and carries Contact us, swinging under the pointer.
options.case: Holds product clarity, because literal labels say exactly what RQ does. It loses on premium identification: luxury streetwear is premium for fashion buyers, not for SME owners.
options.risk: Reads as a fashion-brand costume for a B2B agency, and hazard stripes are an easy cliché.

raised.raise: Sections open by pulling, not fading, and an exposed layer stays exposed as a record.
Every state change snaps one whole step with a single overshoot; nothing glides.
The 3D tag swings with real damped spring physics, never a canned easing curve.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: The page is a lit stage: your operations start in the dark, and scrolling runs the light cues until the whole stage is in daylight.
materials: real light on a modelled curved 3D wall
options.viewport: A full-bleed Three.js curved stage wall in near-black with a low cobalt horizon glowing. The case study's three real objects (an email, a PDF and a folder) stand on stage as silhouetted actors. The headline is set over the horizon with Contact us lit beneath it, and a cue counter in the corner reads CUE 1 · NIGHT.
options.case: Beats the lead on both axes: cinematic and premium without themed props, the biggest real 3D moment in any hand so far, and dark to daylight states the offer without explanation.
options.risk: If the light is a flat CSS gradient instead of real light on a modelled wall, it collapses into the AI aurora-gradient look. The dark opening also leans toward dark tech.

options.label: Man-Machine Wiring
options.thesis: The SME's tools wired into one diagram on a strict grid. Current travels the connectors and lights each lamp as the work automates.
options.viewport: A 3D wireframe grid where Outlook, Excel, Dropbox and invoicing are nodes, and current pulses along orthogonal connectors from node to node. Tight tracked caps carry the headline, and Contact us is the red node.
options.case: Holds product clarity, since integrations are wired literally. It loses on premium identification, because neon on black reads as a band homage and edges toward the dark-neon rut.
options.risk: Neon on black is a cliché, and the design could read as homage rather than identity.

options.label: Torn Billboard
options.thesis: Tear down through older poster layers.
options.viewport: Four campaigns exposed by one tear.
options.case: Fuses poorly: gritty where you asked for premium.
options.kept: Pull to expose, and exposed stays exposed.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.thesis: Cloth courses stepping under one fixed window.
options.viewport: One window with green cloth stopped mid-step.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a monitoring form, neither premium nor 3D.
options.kept: Snap one step with an overshoot; nothing glides.

options.label: Night-Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six calm dials you trust through cloud.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a pilot's instrument panel, not an owner's world, and it invites invented metrics.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light agency site: white ground, near-black type, one accent and product screenshots, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Split hero: headline and buttons on the left, a product visual on the right.
canonCard.risk: Close to the current build and indistinguishable from other agencies by design.
